newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Dow jump sets Australian stocks alight at open.
newsitem.headline: Dow jump sets Australian stocks alight at open.

text.p: The Australian share market sprinted higher at the open on Friday, the market set alight by a resurgent Dow that rocketed to its second-best finish ever.
The All Ordinaries index jumped 24.1 points to 2,355.8 at the open.
Turnover was at impressive levels thanks to the December series options exercises with about A$800 million put through the market prior to the official opening.
Trader's attention was focussed on bellwether BHP which is due to report its interim profit result this morning.
"It's looking good so far after the Dow stormed ahead," said a Sydney broker, adding that the early gains were widespread.
"The miners have had the better of it but everything has gone ahead. It's a broad-based rise."
Market leader BHP was due to report its interim profit result later in the morning and this was exercising the minds of traders, given the company's ability to set the market's overall course.
"BHP is due later on and that could turn the market," the broker said.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about five to one, while about 35 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
